inputs.global_prompt:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the exact same rigid subject shown in <Picture 1>. Its geometry, proportions, materials, colors, markings, and surface details remain unchanged.
<Picture 1> is the first-frame viewpoint of [Shot 1].

summary:
[reference generation] ORB360_CW. A frozen-moment 360-degree orbit of <Subject 1> against the same uniform studio backdrop shown in <Picture 1>, like a single instant stopped in time.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - its geometry, proportions, materials, colors, markings and surface details are retained, and it stays completely frozen.
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame and last frame): fully_preserved - the orbit starts and ends on this view, including its environment, weather and light.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>, with its exact environment, ground, background, weather and light. The camera performs exactly one smooth clockwise 360-degree orbit around the completely stationary <Subject 1>, at constant radius, constant elevation, constant focal length, constant speed, and constant framing, ending at the starting viewpoint. The subject remains perfectly rigid and stationary. The studio backdrop remains flat, seamless and uniform in exactly the original background color from <Picture 1>, throughout all angles. All visible contents retain the reference appearance and stay frozen. This is a clean studio product presentation. No articulation, deformation, secondary motion, wind, zoom, dolly, camera roll, cuts, lighting changes, or scene changes.

All four milestones below belong to the same uninterrupted [Shot 1], not separate shots. The video runs at 24 fps. Angles describe camera motion clockwise as viewed from above, relative to the starting camera azimuth; the subject itself does not rotate. The camera moves continuously at constant angular speed between these milestones, without pausing, reversing or completing extra turns.
At 0.000000 seconds (zero-based frame 0), the camera has advanced 0 degrees clockwise from its starting azimuth; the viewpoint corresponds to <Picture 1>.
At 1.708333 seconds (zero-based frame 41), the camera has advanced 120 degrees clockwise from its starting azimuth.
At 3.416667 seconds (zero-based frame 82), the camera has advanced 240 degrees clockwise from its starting azimuth.
At 5.125000 seconds (zero-based frame 123), the camera has advanced 360 degrees clockwise from its starting azimuth; the viewpoint corresponds to <Picture 1>.

The rigid subject keeps its reference shape, material, proportions and surface details. Only the camera changes position. Camera radius, elevation, focal length and look-at point stay fixed. Lighting stays fixed in world space; normal viewpoint-dependent shading and reflections remain physically consistent.
